title: Quantile Treatment Effect Estimation at Zero Outcome Density with Unknown Design
banked_reason: D0.5 typed review: matched QTE-minimax and honest-length kernels were substituted by upper-only results; independent validity gate found no concrete bounded repair.
gap_reasons: The theorem labeled qte-minimax-frontier supplies only an upper reduction and a generic testing inequality whose load-bearing mixture pair is explicitly unconstructed.
honest-cusp-adaptation proves coverage and upper expected length without optimality.
The projected paper score is further constrained by the absence of evidence that the elaborate third-order procedure materially improves attainable inference beyond its formal upper guarantee.
proof_attempt_summary: The run repaired the third-order estimator by coarse weighted reprojection, proved a no-extra-log unknown-design uniform-CDF upper bound, and obtained valid inverse-cusp QTE and interval upper consequences. Repeated common-channel, continuous-channel, rectangular, and fuzzy-mixture lower-bound routes did not produce a same-class construction valid for every admissible cusp-constant ratio; the common-density route has a proved C/c obstruction. The matched QTE-minimax and honest expected-length converses therefore remained absent, substituting the proposal kernel with an upper-only result below the field floor.
tldr: Coarse weighted reprojection of the clipped inverse-propensity and monotone conditional-CDF pilots closes the deterministic projection leak. The corrected computable unknown-design estimator has threshold-uniform first- and second-moment error \(O(\rho_n)\), including \(u=d/4\). Its seven true-law Hoeffding projections retain every required nuisance factor, while bounded threshold variation follows from the \(L_1\)-stable coarse projection. Fixed-radius inversion can therefore use the CDF premise unconditionally for point estimation, exponent-free coverage, and adaptive upper expected length. No matching unknown-design minimax or same-class expected-length converse is claimed.
gap: Zhang, Liu, and Zhang Theorem 5(ii) proves the below-elbow scalar regular-QTE RMS upper rate \(n^{-(4s/d)/(1+4s/d)}\) for \(0<s/d\le1/4\) under a positive estimating-equation derivative and the paper's projection/Gram conditions. It does not give a threshold-uniform counterfactual-CDF process or cover zero target density. Its Remark 5 specifically says accurate Gram-inverse estimation generally requires additional marginal-density smoothness and leaves the minimax dependence on that smoothness open; empirical-HOIF work removes density smoothness only in the root-n regime. The residual gap is a computable unknown-design no-log slow-rate CDF process and its continuous cusp-minimax consequences.
fill: Define and audit the explicit third-order cross-fold estimator. If all seven true-law projections retain the stated whole-kernel and nuisance-factor bounds, prove the no-log CDF frontier and then matched continuous zero-density QTE risk and honest expected-length frontiers; otherwise report the sharp penalty or model strengthening forced by the failed projection.
